'''Ja'Kobe Amare Walter''' (born September 4, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class.

==Early life and high school career==
Walter grew up in [[McKinney, Texas]] and initially attended [[McKinney High School]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/college/texas/mens-basketball/longhorns-jakobe-walter-visit-austin-chris-beard-commitment-recruit-dillon-mitchell-arterio-morris |title=Elite In-State SG Ja'Kobe Walter Visiting Texas this Weekend |first=Zach |last=Dimmitt |website=[[SI.com]] |date=April 30, 2022 |access-date=February 24, 2023}}</ref> A [[shooting guard]], he averaged 23.3 points, 7.6 rebounds, 1.9 assists, and 2.3 steals per game as a junior leading McKinney to a state championship.<ref>{{cite web |date=June 21, 2022 |title=Baylor lands 5-star shooting guard Ja'Kobe Walter |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4175007/2022/06/22/baylor-lands-5-star-shooting-guard-jakobe-walter/ |access-date=February 24, 2023 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> Walter transferred to [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]] in [[Branson, Missouri]] prior to the start of his senior year.<ref>{{cite web |last=McFarland |first=Shawn |date=May 5, 2022 |title=McKinney five-star junior Ja'Kobe Walter will play final season at Link Academy (Mo.) |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2022/05/05/mckinney-five-star-junior-jakobe-walter-will-play-final-season-at-link-academy-mo/ |access-date=February 23, 2023 |work=[[Dallas Morning News]]}}</ref> Walter was selected to play in the [[2023 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/baylor-signee-walter-named-mcdonalds-all-american/article_8b19a6a2-9c40-11ed-a78b-1fbc6cc3334d.html|title=Baylor signee Walter named McDonald's All-American|work=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]]|date=January 24, 2023|access-date=February 23, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Wert |first=Jason |date=January 27, 2023 |title=Link Academy's Walter to play ===Recruiting===
Walter was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class, according to major recruiting services.<ref>{{cite web |last=McFarland |first=Shawn |date=April 21, 2022 |title=Four Dallas-area freshmen highlight ESPN top 25 boys basketball recruits list for the class of 2025 |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2022/04/21/four-dallas-area-freshmen-highlight-espn-top-25-boys-basketball-recruits-list-for-the-class-of-2025/ |access-date=February 24, 2023 |work=[[Dallas Morning News]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=May 6, 2022 |title=Kansas Jayhawks basketball recruiting update: No. 17 player in 2023 class has KU on list |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article261153192.html |access-date=February 24, 2023 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Article/JaKobe-Walter-Kansas-Texas-Alabama-Auburn-Basketball-Recruiting-187178661/|title=Composite five-star guard Ja'Kobe Walter announces his top eight|first=Brandon|last=Jenkins|website=[[247Sports]]|date=May 4, 2022|access-date=February 24, 2023}}</ref> On June 22, 2022, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] over offers from [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] and [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |author-link2=Paul Biancardi |name-list-style=and |date=June 22, 2022 |title=ESPN 100 recruit Ja'Kobe Walter chooses 'winning history,' will join Baylor men's basketball program |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34132636 |access-date=February 23, 2023 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Walter enrolled at [[Baylor University]] in June 2023 to take part in summer practices.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sicem365.com/s/15219/wingspan-wednesday-summer-basketball-workouts-begin-at-baylor|title=Wingspan Wednesday: Summer Basketball Workouts Begin at Baylor|first=Ashley|last=Hodge|website=Sicem365.com|date=June 14, 2023|access-date=June 26, 2023}}</ref> In his college debut against [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], Walter set the Baylor school record for points in a debut by a freshman, netting 28 on the night.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://247sports.com/college/baylor/article/jakobe-walter-breaks-baylor-freshman-scoring-record-219830092/ | title = Ja'Kobe Walter Breaks Baylor Freshman Scoring Record in Bears season opening win| last = Miner| first = Andrew| date = November 7, 2023|publisher = [[247Sports]]| access-date = November 8, 2023}}</ref> He averaged 14.5 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game. Walter was named [[Big 12]] Freshman of the Year.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Brennan |first1=Brian |title=Sixers draft profile: Ja'Kobe Walter has intriguing shooting, scoring upside |url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/philadelphia-76ers/nba-draft-profile-jakobe-walter-baylor-bears-sixers-nba-draft-2024/585856/ |access-date=July 14, 2024 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=May 21, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 26, 2024, Walter was selected with the 19th overall pick by the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Aaron|last=Rose|title=Raptors Share Excitement & Scouting Report for New 1st Round Pick|url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/toronto-raptors-share-excitement-for-jakobe-walter-following-nba-draft|website=SI.com|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 27, 2024}}</ref> and on July 4, he signed with the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN WALTER, MOGBO AND SHEAD|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-walter-mogbo-and-shead|website=NBA.com|date=July 4, 2024|access-date=July 5, 2024}}</ref> However, he missed the beginning of the season, including training camp, because of an AC joint sprain. Throughout his rookie season, he has been [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to [[Raptors 905]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Raptors 905 Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Raptors-905/41/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 15, 2025}}</ref>

On November 1, 2024, Walter made his NBA debut<ref>{{cite web|last=Taylor|first=Cody|title=Raptors recall Ja'Kobe Walter from G League after productive 905 stint|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/raptors-recall-jakobe-walter-g-015315008.html|website=sports.yahoo.com|date=November 25, 2024|access-date=January 15, 2025}}</ref> and on November 27, he made his first NBA start in his career while achieving his first [[double-double]] with 11 rebounds, 14 points and 5 assists in a 119–93 road win against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Grange|title=Raptors Takeaways: Contributions from entire lineup lead to first road win|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-takeaways-contributions-from-entire-lineup-lead-to-first-road-win/|website=SportsNet.ca|date=November 28, 2024|access-date=January 15, 2025}}</ref> On December 22, he scored a career high of 27 points in a 114-110 home loss against the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Arya|last=Chawla|title=Raptors' Ja'Kobe Walter Erupts For 27 Points Against Houston|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/toronto-raptors-jakobe-walter-erupts-for-27-points-against-rockets|website=Sports Illustrated|date=December 23, 2024|access-date=March 5, 2025}}</ref>

On March 4, 2025, in a 114-113 win against the [[2024–25 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]], Walter had 3 rebounds and scored 17 points, including the game-winning [[Three-point field goal|three]] with 0.5 remaining on the clock in the 4th quarter. This propelled the Raptors to victory on the road at the [[Kia Center]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raptors rookie Ja'Kobe Walter hits 3 with 0.5 seconds left for 114-113 win over slumping Magic|url=https://apnews.com/article/magic-raptors-score-f4f866af8b71b3f14e8359bda540184e|website=AP News|date=March 4, 2025|access-date=March 5, 2025}}</ref>

On May 1, 2026, Walter posted a playoff career high 24 points, along with 5 rebounds and 3 steals, in a 112-110 overtime win against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Koreen |first=Eric |last2=Vardon |first2=Joe |last3=Schubert |first3=Matt |date=May 3, 2026 |title=Raptors outlast Cavaliers with wild last-second 3 in OT, force Game 7: Takeaways |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7247286/2026/05/01/cavaliers-raptors-nba-playoffs-game-6-score-result-takeaways/ |access-date=2026-06-03 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Walter was born and raised in McKinney, Texas, where he has deep family roots. Walter's father, Eddie Walter, played college basketball for [[Birmingham–Southern College]] from 1994 to 1996.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 19, 2024 |title=Ja'Kobe Walter Parents |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/basketball/jakobe-walter-parents#:~:text=Who%20are%20Ja'Kobe%20Walter's,as%20early%20as%20age%205. |access-date=October 8, 2024 |website=Sportskeeda}}</ref> His parents named him after basketball legends [[Kobe Bryant]] and [[Michael Jordan]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=June 26, 2024 |title=Toronto Raptors draft Baylor guard Ja'Kobe Walter 19th overall in NBA Draft |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/article-toronto-raptors-draft-baylor-guard-jakobe-walter-19th-overall-in-nba/#:~:text=Walter's%20first%20name%20Ja'Kobe,be%20drafted%20to%20the%20NBA. |access-date=October 8, 2024 |work=The Globe and Mail |language=en-CA}}</ref> Walter is a Christian and has said that his faith "allowed him to stay humble and use his gifts to serve others".<ref>{{cite web |last=Kruse |first=Ethan |date=January 25, 2023 |title=Ja'Kobe Walter - Keep God First |url=https://hishuddle.com/2023/01/25/jakobe-walter/ |access-date=March 20, 2023 |website=His Huddle}}</ref>
